chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Whichever believer visits a sick believer during his illness in the morning, seventy thousand angels would escort him. So when he sits, mercy would overwhelm him, and they would seek forgiveness from God, Mighty and Majestic, for him until the evening; and if he visits him in the evening, there would be for him the like of that until the morning.

key_terms.اسْتَغْفَرُوا: they sought forgiveness — angels interceding on behalf of the visitor
key_terms.شَيَّعَهُ: escorted/accompanied him — referring to angelic accompaniment
key_terms.عَادَ: visited (the sick) — from 'iyada, the Islamic practice of visiting the ill
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific epithet for God
key_terms.غَمَرَتْهُ الرَّحْمَةُ: mercy overwhelmed/encompassed him — divine mercy enveloping the visitor
key_terms.مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ: the like of that — equal reward for evening visits

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting a sick Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the immense spiritual reward for visiting a sick fellow believer. The act of visiting the sick (known in Islamic tradition as 'iyada) in the morning brings an escort of seventy thousand angels, whose presence fills the visitor with divine mercy and who intercede for him through the day. An evening visit brings equal reward throughout the night. The audience for this teaching were early Shia Muslims in Medina and Kufa, who lived in close-knit communities where caring for the sick was both a social obligation and a means of spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbih who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘Whichever Believer visits a sick Believer in the morning during his illness. Seventy thousand Angels would escort him. So when he sits, the Mercy would overwhelm him, and they would seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic for him until evening; and if he visits him in the evening, there would be for him the like of that until the morning’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from Wahab ibn ‘Abdu Rabbi hi who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘

If a believing person visits a believing patient in his illness in the morning, seventy thousand angels escort him, and when he sits down, mercy covers him altogether and they ask Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, until nightfall to forgive him. If his visit takes place in the evening, similar things happen for him until the next morning.’”
